div.l: A Person̄A Good man vas ther / of Religion̄
And was a pore ꝑperson / of a toun
But Riche he was / of holy thought and werk
He was also a lernyd man / a clerk ·
That cristes gospel / treuly wold preche
His parisshenys / deuoutly wold he teche
Benygne he was / and wondyr dyligent
And in adủersyte / wol pacyent
And such he was p̉erued / ofte sythes
For loth he was / to cursen for his tythes
But rather wold he yeven / out of doute
Vn to his pore parisshenys / a boute
Of his offryng / and of his sustynaıı̄unce
He covde in lytel thynges / have suffisaunce
Wyde was his parissh and houses fer asondyr
But he laft nat / for reyn ne for thondyr
In seknesse ne in myscheff / to vysyte
The ferthest in his parysh mochil and lyte
Vpon his feet / and in his hand a staf
This noble ensample / to his sheep he yaf
And ferst he wrought / and aftyrward he tawghte
Oute of the gospel / he tho wordys cawghte
And this figure / he Addyd eke ther to
Yf gold rust / what shal Iren do
For yf a prest be foul . / on whom we truste
No wondyr is / a lewde man to ruste
And shame it is / if a prest take keep
A shetene shepperde / and a clene shep
Wel awthe a prest / ensample for to yeven
By his clennesse / how his sheep shuld leven
He set nat his benefys / to hire
And leet his sheep / accombre in the myre
And ran vn to londone / vn to seynt Poulis
